topics.topic: Whether prototypes are prohibited, optional, or non-authoritative in later design layers
questions: Are later layers prohibited from using a prototype, or is the former requirement merely withdrawn so that a prototype remains optional?
Is using a prototype to answer a later layer’s open questions prohibited, or is it merely no longer required?
Is using a prototype prohibited, merely no longer mandatory, or allowed only as non-authoritative evidence?

quotes:
The decision of 2026-11-18 to fill each layer through a running prototype is withdrawn. Each
layer is written from the layers before it and the owner's decisions, by the rules of its own
state. A claim with no owner decision is an open question.
judgement.why: The text withdraws the prototype mandate and makes prototypes non-authoritative: later layers derive claims from prior layers and owner decisions, while undecided claims remain open.

topics.topic: Camera-record fields, precedence, and validity rules
questions: Which embedded fields constitute the camera record, what is their precedence when they disagree, and what makes a field absent or invalid?

quotes:
The photo moment is the first usable value of: EXIF `DateTimeOriginal`, EXIF `DateTime`, then
the file's modification time. `DateTimeOriginal` uses `OffsetTimeOriginal` when that offset matches
the imported `EXIF_OFFSET_PATTERN` constant whole, with hours up to the imported `CAMERA_OFFSET_MAX_HOURS` constant and minutes that are a minute of the hour; otherwise it is read in the time zone of the `timezone` field of the run settings (A8), and so is
`DateTime`. A camera value is unusable when it does not match the imported `EXIF_DATETIME_PATTERN` constant whole or is no valid calendar date and time, when its UTC year
is before the imported `CAMERA_EARLIEST_YEAR` constant, or when it is more than the imported
`CAMERA_LATEST_AFTER_MODIFIED_HOURS` constant of hours after the file's modification time.
judgement.why: State 2 specifies the camera fields, their precedence, offset handling and all validity conditions.

topics.topic: Contract status of the Portal's missing intake_id
questions: Is the absence of `intake_id` a guaranteed production Portal contract, a current observation that must be revalidated, or an assumption the design must tolerate becoming false?

quotes:
While a photo is hidden, a flow that lost the Portal's answer repeats the publication and
receives the same `photo_id`. After the owner has shown the photo the Portal answers 409, and
the `photo_id` of an unmarked photo cannot be recovered from the Portal. This is a recorded
limit of the first version.
judgement.why: State 2 treats inability to recover the photo id from the Portal as a recorded first-version limit on which the flow must rely.

questions: What constitutes identical source content: raw file bytes, decoded pixels, pixels after orientation, or the prepared image after metadata removal and resizing?

quotes: A placement is identified by the project and the SHA-256 of the source content (R0-10).

A named file that passes condition 1 of rule 5 is judged by A1 orders 1 to 6 and read once; the bytes
that were read are the bytes judged, hashed and prepared.
judgement.why: State 2 defines source identity as the SHA-256 of the raw bytes read from the source file, before preparation.

topics.topic: Repeated-publication 409 conditions, response, and caller semantics
questions: Exactly which repeated-publication states produce 409, what response identifies the existing photo, and must the caller treat that response as success, conflict, or failure?

quotes:
While a photo is hidden, a flow that lost the Portal's answer repeats the publication and
receives the same `photo_id`. After the owner has shown the photo the Portal answers 409, and
the `photo_id` of an unmarked photo cannot be recovered from the Portal. This is a recorded
limit of the first version.

The agent makes one attempt per photo in a run and does not retry by itself. The owner starts another run, and repeating
is safe: a run stopped between publishing and marking repeats while the photo is hidden, because the Portal returns the
same `photo_id`. If the owner has shown the photo first, `photo.publish` answers 409 and the photo fails with the reason
that the owner already showed it, because its `photo_id` cannot be recovered from the Portal (A4 rule 5). The service
keeps no state of a run, so nothing is left to clean up.
judgement.why: States 2 and 4 distinguish hidden-photo replay from post-showing 409 and require the latter to be reported as failure because no existing photo id is recoverable.

questions: What output formats, color-profile handling, animation handling, resize method and encoding quality define the stored image, and what happens when an input cannot be converted?

quotes:
A stored image is a newly encoded JPEG made from the decoded pixels of the first frame of the source by
exactly these operations of the image library at the version A9 pins, in this order, whose arithmetic
(conversion formulas, resampling, rounding of sizes, alpha compositing and encoding) is that library's:
its EXIF transposition applies the camera orientation; its conversion to RGBA converts the decoded
samples, without colour management and without a colour profile; its thumbnail reduction with the
LANCZOS filter to a box of the imported `PHOTO_MAX_SIDE` constant on each side reduces the image when a
side is larger than that box, keeping its proportion; the result is pasted onto an RGB image of the same
size filled with the colour of the imported `PHOTO_BACKGROUND` constant, with its own alpha channel as
the mask, so transparent areas take that colour; and its JPEG encoding writes the image with quality the
imported `PHOTO_QUALITY` constant, optimize the imported `PHOTO_OPTIMIZE` constant, progressive the
imported `PHOTO_PROGRESSIVE` constant and subsampling the imported `PHOTO_SUBSAMPLING` constant, with no
EXIF, colour profile or other metadata. With one library version one source gives the same bytes. `sha256`
and `size` of M04 describe the bytes that were stored, its `media_type` is the imported `STORED_MEDIA_TYPE` constant, and a repeated delivery returns that placement
without encoding again (A3 rule 2).

The source may be of a format of the imported `SOURCE_FORMATS` constant. A scan decides membership by the
signature alone (A1 order 6). Decoding is the image library's, restricted to the formats of that constant:
which of them it detects is the library's decision. A source it cannot open as one of them fails with the
UNREADABLE_IMAGE member of = models.PlacementFailure, whatever dimensions its header declares. For a source
it opens, checks run in this order: a first frame whose width times height is above the imported
`MAX_PIXELS` constant fails with the TOO_MANY_PIXELS member of = models.PlacementFailure, a source that cannot be decoded with the
UNREADABLE_IMAGE member of = models.PlacementFailure, and a result longer than the imported `MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES` constant, the Portal's
read limit, with the TOO_LARGE member of = models.PlacementFailure. A value equal to a limit passes. Only the first frame of an animated
image is delivered.
judgement.why: State 2 fully specifies JPEG conversion, color and alpha handling, animation behavior, resizing, encoding controls and conversion failures.

topics.topic: Syncthing incomplete-file naming guarantees and exclusion patterns
questions: Is Syncthing guaranteed to keep every incomplete file under an ignored temporary name until an atomic final rename, across the deployed version, filesystem and VPS configuration?
What exact names or patterns count as a Syncthing temporary file or hidden name, and is matching based on every path component or only the file basename?

quotes:
A name is ignored at every level of the path when, after the letters A to Z are lowered and no other
character is changed, it begins with an item of the imported `IGNORED_NAME_PREFIXES` constant, ends with
an item of the imported `IGNORED_NAME_SUFFIXES` constant, or contains the imported `CONFLICT_COPY_MARK`
constant, the mark of a Syncthing conflict copy (R0-14). Names beginning with a dot include Syncthing's
`.syncthing.*`, `.stfolder` and `.stversions` and the phone's `.trashed-*` files. A file Syncthing is still
writing lies under such a temporary name. Ignored names are not reported, ignored folders are not entered,
and an entry the listing shows as a symbolic link is neither reported nor followed.

Syncthing may change the folder during a scan, so a scan is not a view of one instant. Each folder is
listed once, in one pass over its entries; an entry added or removed during that pass may or may not be
among them. Each rule applies
to what its step finds when it runs, and the next scan sees the folder as it then stands. A file that
changes while it is read is judged by the bytes that were read, once, without a retry. Syncthing replaces
a finished file by renaming a new one over it; a later delivery judges what it then reads under A3 rule 5.
judgement.why: State 2 makes the temporary-name and finished-file replacement assumptions normative and defines the exact case-folded patterns at every path level, including hidden directories.

topics.topic: Timezone used to convert timezone-less timestamps to UTC
questions: How is a camera or filesystem timestamp with no timezone converted to UTC, and which timezone applies when the source device, project and VPS differ?

quotes:
The photo date is delivered as UTC without an offset, as the Client Portal stores it. A camera
time with no offset is read in the time zone of that `timezone` field. A local time that occurs twice is the
first occurrence, and a local time that does not exist is read with the offset in force before
the clock change. A modification time is an absolute instant converted to UTC.
judgement.why: State 2 requires timezone-less camera values to use the configured service timezone and gives Europe/Madrid as its default.
